report.summary: Review of lib/source-visibility-probe.ts, lib/saved-page-observation.ts and tests/source-visibility-browser-fixture.mjs. The ancestor display:none / opacity:0 / content-visibility:hidden checks and the own-parent visibility check handle the reported override case correctly, and the five cited fixture outcomes follow from the CSS. Two concrete defects remain: (1) the ancestor scan starts at the text's direct parent, so an inert ancestor (or an inert text parent) is reported visible; the fixture has no opacity:0 ancestor with a visibility:visible child, so this regression path is not exercised; (2) the probe calls win.scrollTo but discards the returned Range rect, so text in a normal in-flow ancestor that is scrolled out of its own viewport is still reported visible. Cancellation and snapshot handling look bounded and use the existing assertCurrent/verifyStyles/local-abort design; the fixture result endpoint does not validate that the POSTed delivery/assessment IDs match the planned snapshot, but no target-source defect beyond that was identified. No code was executed; all statements are static analysis.

findings.title: Ancestor suppression scan omits inert and skips child-restored visibility cases inconsistently with visible()
findings.evidence: Lines 29-36 inspect only visibility (own parent only) and, for each ancestor from node.parentElement upward, display, opacity and contentVisibility. Line 30 returns hidden when the parent's visibility is hidden/collapse, but a child can restore visibility:visible under an inert (or visibility-visible) ancestor. An `inert` ancestor makes all its descendants non-rendered/non-visible to assistive tech and to hit-testing; the current probe has no `hasAttribute("inert")` check, whereas lib/saved-page-observation.ts:106 (visible()) does check `current.hasAttribute("inert")`. A citation whose text sits inside `.card[inert] p` (no CSS hiding) gets ownStyle.visibility=visible, no display/opacity/content hidden ancestor, a non-zero range rect within the viewport (inert does not collapse layout), and is classified `visible` though it is inert. Similarly the loop checks contentVisibility==="hidden" on every ancestor but does not account for `content-visibility:visible` overrides or `content-visibility:auto` skipped-subtree state; more concretely, the fixture cannot catch the opacity case because it has no opacity:0 ancestor with a visibility:visible child (css line 12 has `.transparent{opacity:0}` on the parent of `.revealed`, whose parent has visibility:visible everywhere, and line 29 scans that ancestor so it is caught only because the fixture's `.revealed` opacity is 1, i.e., the test accidentally exercises only the ancestor-opacity suppression for a non-visibility-restoring child).
findings.reproduction:
Static trace (unexecuted): add `

Current hours eleven to eight

` to the fixture body and remove the main copy of that text; target path resolves to the p, ownStyle.visibility='visible', ancestors have no display:none/opacity:0/contentVisibility:hidden, range rect is in-viewport, so observeCitationText returns {state:'visible'} while the element is inert. Also: add CSS `.anc{opacity:0}.anc p{visibility:visible}` with the target text inside; the ancestor scan catches opacity:0, but if a future refactor mirrors visible() and checks visibility along the chain it would regress, so the fixture's '.transparent .revealed' case does not cover an opacity ancestor with a child that also restores visibility.
findings.suggestion: Add `if(element.hasAttribute("inert")) return {state:"hidden",reason:"inert"}` (and, if a reason exists, an equivalent check for aria-hidden only if the contract treats it as hidden) inside the ancestor loop at line 31-36, and extend the fixture with an inert ancestor case plus an `opacity:0` ancestor containing a `visibility:visible` child to lock the interaction between the two suppression rules.

findings.title: Rect test ignores scroll containers after scrolling only the top window
findings.evidence: Line 38 calls `win.scrollTo({top:...})` on the iframe window and then line 39 reads `range.getClientRects()`; line 40 accepts any rect that intersects the iframe viewport. If the cited text is inside an ancestor with `overflow:auto/scroll` and the ancestor's scroll position leaves the text outside the ancestor's client box, the text's rect may still lie within the iframe viewport (e.g., a tall scroller whose top is above the text or a horizontally scrolled container), so the probe reports `visible` even though the text is clipped and not visible to a user without scrolling the inner container. The probe only ever scrolls the document window, never the nearest scrollable ancestor, and never checks ancestor clip rectangles (overflow hidden/clip, fixed-height containers).
findings.reproduction:
Static trace (unexecuted): fixture HTML `

Current hours eleven to eight

` places the paragraph below the scroller's visible box; the container is 40px tall, so the paragraph's rect starts below the container bottom but remains within the LAYOUT_HEIGHT iframe viewport below it if the scroller is near the top; window scrollTo moves the whole page, not the scroller scrollTop, so the paragraph rect still falls in the viewport and the classifier returns `visible` while a user sees only the 40px scroller window (unless the paragraph happens to be pushed off the iframe viewport by other content, which is not guaranteed).
findings.suggestion: Before accepting a rect, walk the target's scrollable/clipping ancestors and require each rect to intersect each ancestor's client box (or, at minimum, replicate a bounded scroll-into-view of the nearest scrollable ancestor and re-measure), or return `not_visually_determined` when an ancestor has overflow not `visible` and the rect is clipped by it.

findings.title: Fixture /result accepts arbitrary delivery/assessment IDs from the POST body
findings.evidence: Line 26 calls `createSourceVisibilityReport(quote,"buyer",JSON.parse(body))` with the body supplied by the browser page. Line 15 posts `{deliveryId:data.plan.deliveryId,assessmentId:data.plan.assessmentId,...}` but the server does not compare these with `plan`/`quote` (line 14 computes `plan` from the same quote in-process). A tampered or stale client could post readings attributed to a different deliveryId/assessmentId, and the reported `result.json` would be generated without demonstrating the intended binding; only if createSourceVisibilityReport validates these against the quote (not in packet) would this be caught. This weakens the fixture as evidence that the probe result is bound to the observed snapshot.
findings.reproduction: Static trace (unexecuted): POST /result with body `{"deliveryId":"other","assessmentId":"other","readings":[...]}`; the fixture does not reject before line 26 and would call createSourceVisibilityReport with the forged IDs.
findings.suggestion: In the /result handler (before line 26), reject unless `body.deliveryId===plan.deliveryId && body.assessmentId===plan.assessmentId` (HTTP 400), so the fixture proves the report is saved only for the observed plan snapshot.

limitations: Only the four supplied packet files were inspected; lib/source-visibility.ts, contracts.ts, layout-probe.ts, layout-report.ts, createSourceVisibilityReport and sourceVisibilityPlan were not available, so their validation of states/reasons and ID binding is unverified.
No code was executed: no unit tests, typecheck, Vite build, browser run or CUA session was performed; the supplied CUA results at 375/1280 were taken as reported, not re-verified.

The inert finding assumes the product intends inert content to be non-visible for this classifier (consistent with lib/saved-page-observation.ts:106 visible()); if the contract deliberately treats inert as merely non-interactive, the severity should be downgraded, but the probe still lacks any documentation or test for that choice.

The scroll-container finding is a static reasoning trace; actual clipping behavior depends on whether the cited rect was pushed outside the iframe viewport by surrounding content, which was not measured.
Classification limits per packet: these are participant-reported static layout observations from a local fixture, not live attestation, overlay/accessibility/usability findings, or acceptance.
